Fictional individual customers. A person's date of birth is given as an age rule, and the harness works out the real date when it seeds them (today minus age_years minus days_past_birthday), so the age a case expects stays correct whenever it is run. CNICs are well-formed but made up and are not placeholder sequences.

A small individual plan catalog with fixed numbers, so eligibility, income-multiple and premium expectations do not depend on whatever plans a real tenant holds. The numbers are evaluation inputs, not any insurer's product terms. Rates follow the platform's own per-1,000 convention.

Proposals, issued policies and their status history, so lifecycle and claims cases start from a fixed record. In-force dates are absolute on purpose: claim eligibility depends on the gap between inception, lapse, reinstatement and the event, not on today's date. Proposal-stage policies use plain statuses and let the harness date them. A claim's reported date is the day it is registered, so cases that register a claim give the event date as a date relative to the run (a {{date:today-4d}} token in the message), which keeps them correct whenever they run.
Synthetic salary slip: monthly gross PKR 100,000 (PKR 1,200,000 a year), which agrees with Ayesha's declared income.
Synthetic salary slip: monthly gross PKR 60,000 (PKR 720,000 a year), 40% below Ayesha's declared PKR 1,200,000.
Two isolated evaluation tenants and one synthetic user per role. Cases name users by ref. Nothing here exists in production; the harness creates it in a dedicated sandbox and removes it afterwards.
